text.p: Swiss shares broke from an early rise, ending weaker in quiet trade as a technical reaction to Tuesday's massive slump wore off during the course of the day.
"After three good months, we may be in for a period of stagnation," one dealer said, noting that U.S. interest rate fears were likely to keep the lid on markets.
He said the early rebound after Tuesday's three percent fall was not convincing and that investors took profits in late trade.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index lost 13.0 points, or 0.29 percent, to end at 4,488.7 and the all-share SPI was down 4.68 points to 2,851.55.
Volume was described as relatively high. Bourse turnover stood at 1.96 billion Swiss francs.
One dealer said that although prospects did not look too bright, there were still few alternatives to shares. Many investors were also seen waiting for U.S. employment data, due on Friday.
Index heavyweight Roche was actively traded, sliding 200 francs, or 1.68 percent, to 11,725. Novartis registered shares gave up five francs to finish at 1,773.
Insurer Winterthur and inspection firm Surveillance, which saw sizeable losses on Tuesday, rebounded strongly. Winterthur jumped 22 francs to 991 and Surveillance climbed 85 francs to 2,910.
CS Group, which had posted a slump of more than five percent on Tuesday, closed flat at 163.25. UBS bearer shares gave up four francs to close at 1,245.

Swissair fell two francs to 1,248. SAirGroup, Swissair's holding company, is due to release its 1996 results on Friday. Analysts expected a net loss of around 108 million francs compared with 1995's loss of 147 million francs.
